prompt: What are the most useful keyboard shortcuts in Office?
completion:
Here are some of the most useful keyboard shortcuts for Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook):

### **General Office Shortcuts**
- **Ctrl + S** – Save the current file.
- **Ctrl + O** – Open a file.
- **Ctrl + P** – Print the current document.
- **Ctrl + N** – Create a new document.
- **Ctrl + Z** – Undo the last action.
- **Ctrl + Y** – Redo the last undone action.
- **F12** – Open the "Save As" dialog box.
- **Ctrl + F** – Find text in the document.
- **Ctrl + H** – Replace text in the document.
- **Ctrl + A** – Select all content.
- **Ctrl + C** – Copy selected text/object.
- **Ctrl + X** – Cut selected text/object.
- **Ctrl + V** – Paste the copied/cut text/object.
- **Alt + F8** – Open the Macro dialog box.

### **Microsoft Word Shortcuts**
- **Ctrl + B** – Bold selected text.
- **Ctrl + I** – Italicize selected text.
- **Ctrl + U** – Underline selected text.
- **Ctrl + D** – Open the Font dialog box.
- **Ctrl + L** – Left-align text.
- **Ctrl + E** – Center-align text.
- **Ctrl + R** – Right-align text.
- **Ctrl + J** – Justify text.
- **Ctrl + M** – Indent a paragraph.
- **Ctrl + Shift + >** – Increase font size.
- **Ctrl + Shift + <** – Decrease font size.
- **Ctrl + Shift + C** – Copy formatting.
- **Ctrl + Shift + V** – Paste formatting.
- **Ctrl + [** – Decrease font size by 1 point.
- **Ctrl + ]** – Increase font size by 1 point.
- **Ctrl + Shift + D** – Copy text to next slide (PowerPoint).
- **Ctrl + K** – Insert a hyperlink.
- **Ctrl + Shift + F12** – Print the current document.

### **Microsoft Excel Shortcuts**
- **Ctrl + ;** – Insert current date.
- **Ctrl + Shift + :** – Insert current time.
- **Ctrl + D** – Fill down (copy cell content downward).
- **Ctrl + R** – Fill right (copy cell content to the right).
- **Ctrl + Shift + =** – Insert a formula (AutoSum).
- **Ctrl + T** – Create a table from selected data.
- **Ctrl + 1** – Open the Format Cells dialog box.
- **Ctrl + Shift + L** – Apply or remove filters.
- **Ctrl + Page Up** – Move to the previous sheet.
- **Ctrl + Page Down** – Move to the next sheet.
- **F2** – Edit the selected cell.
- **Ctrl + '** – Copy the formula from the cell above.
- **Ctrl + Shift + +** – Insert a new row or column.
- **Ctrl + -** – Delete the selected row or column.
- **Ctrl + Space** – Select the entire column.
- **Shift + Space** – Select the entire row.

### **Microsoft PowerPoint Shortcuts**
- **Ctrl + M** – Insert a new slide.
- **Ctrl + D** – Duplicate the selected slide.
- **Ctrl + G** – Group selected objects.
- **Ctrl + Shift + G** – Ungroup selected objects.
- **Ctrl + K** – Insert a hyperlink.
- **Ctrl + Shift + C** – Copy formatting.
- **Ctrl + Shift + V** – Paste formatting.
- **F5** – Start the slideshow from the beginning.
- **Shift + F5** – Start the slideshow from the current slide.
- **Esc** – Exit slideshow mode.

### **Microsoft Outlook Shortcuts**
- **Ctrl + N** – Create a new email.
- **Ctrl + Shift + A** – Create a new appointment.
- **Ctrl + R** – Reply to an email.
- **Ctrl + Shift + R** – Reply to all.
- **Ctrl + F** – Forward an email.
- **Ctrl + E** – Open the Search bar.
- **Ctrl + Enter** – Send the current email.
- **Ctrl + Shift + M** – Create a new meeting request.
- **Ctrl + 1** – Switch to Mail view.
- **Ctrl + 2** – Switch to Calendar view.
- **Ctrl + 3** – Switch to Contacts view.
- **Ctrl + 4** – Switch to Tasks view.
- **Ctrl + 5** – Switch to Notes view.

These shortcuts can significantly speed up your workflow in Microsoft Office applications.
